title: Ninth Word Fifth Point Human Weakness Impotence And Needs

questions.question: How does the passage describe a person’s natural strength?
questions.answer: It says a person is very weak by nature.

questions.question: What effect do many things in life have on a person’s heart?
questions.answer: They can hurt him and make him feel sad.

questions.question: How is a person’s power described?
questions.answer: It is described as very small.

questions.question: What is said about the troubles and enemies a person faces?
questions.answer: They are many.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about human needs?
questions.answer: A person has a lot of needs.

questions.question: How does the passage describe a person’s ability to carry out work?
questions.answer: It says he is slow and not very able.

questions.question: What is said about the duties of life?
questions.answer: They are heavy and hard to carry.

questions.question: How does being human connect a person to other things?
questions.answer: It links him to the whole universe.

questions.question: Why do change and loss cause pain to a person?
questions.answer: Because he loves familiar things, and it hurts when they fade away or disappear.

questions.question: What does a person’s mind show him?
questions.answer: It shows him high goals and lasting results.

questions.question: What limits keep a person from reaching all those goals easily?
questions.answer: His ability is limited, his life is short, his strength is small, and his patience is not great.

questions.question: What is one main idea of the whole passage?
questions.answer: Human beings have many weaknesses, needs, and limits.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kind of condition is a human being in?
questions.answer: A human being is in a needy, weak, and limited condition.

questions.question: What two feelings can come when many things affect a person deeply?
questions.answer: Grief and sadness.

questions.question: Which is greater in the passage: human power or the number of hardships?
questions.answer: The number of hardships is greater.

questions.question: What contrast does the passage make about human need?
questions.answer: It shows that a person has little in himself but needs many things.

questions.question: How does the passage compare a person’s ability with life’s duties?
questions.answer: It says a person is not very capable, but life’s duties are very heavy.

questions.question: What part of being human makes losses hurt more?
questions.answer: Being connected to the world around him makes those losses hurt more.

questions.question: What happens when things a person loves go away?
questions.answer: He feels pain again and again.

questions.question: What does reason help a person notice?
questions.answer: It helps him notice noble goals and lasting rewards.

questions.question: Why might a person struggle to reach those goals?
questions.answer: Because his reach is limited, his life is short, and he does not have much strength or patience.

questions.question: Does the passage paint human life as easy or challenging? Explain briefly.
questions.answer: Challenging, because people face many troubles, needs, duties, and losses.

questions.question: What idea about human nature is repeated in several ways?
questions.answer: That people are limited and cannot rely on themselves completely.

questions.question: What is the first weakness about people mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: People are naturally very weak.

questions.question: Besides weakness, what does the passage say about human power?
questions.answer: It says people have very little power.

questions.question: What comes against people even though they have little power?
questions.answer: Many disasters and enemies come against them.

questions.question: What does the passage say about what people lack?
questions.answer: It says they are full of wants and do not have enough.

questions.question: How many needs does the passage say people have?
questions.answer: It says they have many needs.

questions.question: What does the passage say about human energy and skill?
questions.answer: It says people can be sluggish and not fully able.

questions.question: Are life’s responsibilities described as light or heavy?
questions.answer: They are described as heavy.

questions.question: What wider connection comes with being human?
questions.answer: A person becomes connected with the rest of creation.

questions.question: How do the loss and passing of familiar things affect a person?
questions.answer: They keep causing him pain.

questions.question: What kind of goals does the mind point toward?
questions.answer: Great and lofty goals.

questions.question: What four limits are named near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Limited reach, short life, small power, and little patience.

questions.question: In the passage, what makes a person easy to be affected by many things?
questions.answer: His weakness makes him easy to be affected.

questions.question: When troubles are many and strength is small, what does that show about people?
questions.answer: It shows that people are not self-sufficient.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the number of enemies and hardships around a person?
questions.answer: It describes them as very numerous.

questions.question: What mismatch does the passage show between what people have and what they need?
questions.answer: They have little, but they need a lot.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the relationship between human ability and life’s burden?
questions.answer: Human ability is limited, but life’s burden is hard to carry.

questions.question: Why do familiar things matter so much to a person in this passage?
questions.answer: Because he becomes attached to them and loves them.

questions.question: What causes ongoing emotional pain according to the passage?
questions.answer: Seeing loved and familiar things decline and disappear.

questions.question: What good things does reason show to a person?
questions.answer: It shows noble goals and lasting outcomes.

questions.question: What keeps a person from easily reaching everything reason points to?
questions.answer: His reach is short, his life is brief, and his strength and patience are limited.

questions.question: What tone does the passage have about human nature: proud or humble?
questions.answer: Humble.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the basic condition of human beings?
questions.answer: Human beings are weak, needy, and limited.

questions.question: What happens because many things touch a person’s life and heart?
questions.answer: He becomes upset and sorrowful.

questions.question: Even though people are low in power, what is high in number?
questions.answer: Their hardships and enemies.

questions.question: What does the passage say about what people want and need?
questions.answer: It says their wants and needs are many.

questions.question: What two words in the passage show that people may struggle to act strongly?
questions.answer: It describes them as lazy and incapable.

questions.question: What is difficult about life besides its troubles?
questions.answer: Its duties are also hard to bear.

questions.question: How does being human increase a person’s pain when things change?
questions.answer: It ties him to many things, so their loss hurts him.

questions.question: What kind of things does a person often love in the passage?
questions.answer: Things he knows well and feels close to.

questions.question: What does reason let a person see beyond everyday life?
questions.answer: It lets him see higher purposes and lasting benefits.

questions.question: Why is there a struggle between what a person hopes for and what he can do?
questions.answer: Because his hopes are big, but his ability and time are small.

questions.question: Which human quality is said to be small along with power?
questions.answer: Patience.

questions.question: What picture of the human being does the passage give at the start?
questions.answer: It gives the picture of a very weak person.

questions.question: What emotional result comes from being affected by many things?
questions.answer: A person feels hurt, sad, and weighed down.

questions.question: What does the passage say about human strength against danger?
questions.answer: Human strength is very small compared to the dangers.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about human poverty in a broad sense?
questions.answer: It teaches that people do not have enough in themselves and need many things.

questions.question: What makes life hard even if a person wants to do well?
questions.answer: Life places heavy responsibilities on him.

questions.question: How far does human connection reach according to the passage?
questions.answer: It reaches out to the whole universe.

questions.question: What repeated experience brings pain to a person’s heart?
questions.answer: The fading and loss of things he loves and recognizes.

questions.question: What can the human mind understand that goes beyond daily survival?
questions.answer: It can understand high goals and lasting results.

questions.question: What shortness or smallness is mentioned about human life and ability?
questions.answer: A person’s reach is short, his life is short, and his power is slight.

questions.question: How does little patience add to human difficulty?
questions.answer: It makes it harder to keep going through long struggles and heavy duties.

questions.question: If you had to choose one word for the human condition in this passage, what word fits best?
questions.answer: Neediness.
